clue.text: Run around a little — it won't do much harm

indicators.note: around tells us the word for run is wrapped about the other piece

parts.note: to run away is to flee
a little means a bit

explanation.surface: Advice to dash about briefly, reassured that it causes no real harm.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny insect bite is the stock example of a trivial, harmless injury or nuisance.

clue.text: Bouncer for the dance

definitions.meaning: something that bounces, a toy sphere

explanation.definitionFit: A ball both bounces and is a grand formal dance, two unrelated senses of one word.

clue.text: Army officer with what may be an excuse for a dog

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel
an excuse may be an untruth, a fib

explanation.surface: A military man offering a dodgy excuse involving a dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A collie is a breed of sheepdog, so this is an example of a dog.

clue.text: Whole triangle is out of kilter

indicators.note: something out of kilter is disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Integral can mean complete or entire, a whole made of its necessary parts.

clue.text: City's victory over another

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits over the second one

parts.note: a victory is a win
another city, Chester in north-west England

explanation.surface: A football report: one city's team triumphs over a rival city's.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s on City is 'is', joining definition to wordplay. Chester is a cathedral city in Cheshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Winchester is a cathedral city in Hampshire, the former capital of Wessex.

clue.text: No big shot in the gunnery world

definitions.text: No big shot in the gunnery world

parts.words: No big shot in the gunnery world
parts.note: a big shot is an important person, but read literally it is a large projectile; this is a tiny one fired from a gun

explanation.definitionFit: A pellet is a small piece of lead shot fired from an airgun or shotgun.

clue.text: Fish from Barcelona with no name

indicators.note: from signals the fish is made out of the letters of the city that remain
with no means a letter is left out of the city name

explanation.surface: A fish caught off the Spanish coast, unnamed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no name' takes the N out of BARCELONA, leaving BARCELOA, and 'from' rearranges those eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The albacore is a long-finned tuna, a kind of fish.

clue.text: Mistakes are holding sailor up

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the whole assembly is read from the bottom
holding means the first word encloses the next one

parts.note: a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Errors are keeping a seaman from departing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' sets the sailor inside the word given, and 'up' then turns the whole six-letter assembly over, as a down answer reads bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata is the Latin plural for errors, especially those listed in a printed book.

clue.text: Is included amongst those who are against rackets

indicators.note: included amongst means the first piece goes inside the next

parts.note: in a vote, those against are the noes

explanation.surface: Something is counted among opponents of tennis bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rackets' looks like the tennis bats; here it means din.
explanation.definitionFit: A racket is a loud din, so rackets are loud sounds.

clue.text: Post of bodyguard

definitions.meaning: letters and parcels delivered by the postal service
armour of linked rings, which guards the body

explanation.definitionFit: Mail is both the postal delivery and chain armour protecting the body.

clue.text: Extensive weighbridge

definitions.meaning: read literally, a big weighing machine for lorries

explanation.definitionFit: Large-scale means extensive; a weighbridge is literally a big set of scales.

clue.text: Scurvy taking hold of sailor? It's not impossible

indicators.note: taking hold of means the first word grips the second inside it

parts.note: scurvy as an adjective means contemptible, vile
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Could a sailor really catch scurvy? It's possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scurvy' looks like the disease, but it is the old adjective meaning base.
explanation.definitionFit: Something viable is workable or feasible, the opposite of impossible.

clue.text: Edna's kebab is mixed with cheap tinned food

indicators.note: mixed means the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Edna's kebab gets a side of canned food stirred in.
explanation.definitionFit: Baked beans in tomato sauce are a cheap, popular canned food.

clue.text: Hills split internally by floods

indicators.note: internally means the second piece goes inside the first

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor
a rent is a split or tear

explanation.surface: Hillsides cleft from inside by floodwater.
explanation.definitionFit: Torrents are violent rushing streams, so a synonym of floods.

clue.text: Man comes in to work in the garden for a couple of days

indicators.note: comes in means the man's name goes inside the other word

parts.note: to weed is to work in the garden
Ken is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man arrives to do gardening for two days.
explanation.definitionFit: The weekend is Saturday and Sunday, two days.

clue.text: It didn't take single boarders

parts.note: boarders sounds like lodgers, but these passengers came aboard in pairs, two of every kind of animal

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the animals entered the ark two by two, so none came singly.

clue.text: Summed up, keeping nothing secret

definitions.meaning: in total, when everything is counted
read literally, everything has been told

explanation.definitionFit: All told means in total, and literally everything has been told.

clue.text: With hindsight, she became a seasoned columnist

definitions.text: With hindsight, she became a seasoned columnist

parts.words: With hindsight, she became a seasoned columnist
parts.note: she looked back and was turned into a column that is salted, seasoned literally

explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis this woman looked back at Sodom and was turned into a pillar of salt.

clue.text: Pineapple found in the banana split

indicators.note: found in means the letters sit inside the run of words

explanation.surface: A pineapple turns up in the banana dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananas is the botanical genus name for pineapple, used as the word in French.

clue.text: Pollution caused by a Channel Islands sewer

parts.note: a sewer is a drain

explanation.surface: Pollution blamed on a sewage pipe in Jersey or Guernsey.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid rain is rainfall made acidic by atmospheric pollutants, a form of pollution.

clue.text: One brass instrument that clashes with another

definitions.text: One brass instrument that clashes with another

parts.words: One brass instrument that clashes with another
parts.note: clashes suggests a disagreement, but this is a brass disc struck against its partner

explanation.definitionFit: A cymbal is a brass percussion disc, often played by striking a pair together.

clue.text: One enrolled in group to get equal pay

indicators.note: enrolled in means the first piece joins and sits inside the group

parts.note: a party is a group
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A member joining a union to win the same wages.
explanation.definitionFit: Parity means equality, especially equal status or pay between groups.

clue.text: Support for a head in retirement

definitions.text: Support for a head in retirement

parts.words: Support for a head in retirement
parts.note: retirement suggests a pensioned headteacher, but means going to bed

explanation.definitionFit: A pillow cushions the head when one retires to bed.

clue.text: Prison meal served up cold

indicators.note: served up suggests food dished out, here the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jail dinner is dished out cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Impersonal means cold and detached, lacking warmth.

clue.text: Weapons some people play with

definitions.meaning: violinists and cellists play with these rods

explanation.definitionFit: Bows are both archery weapons and the rods used to play stringed instruments.

clue.text: Man-of-war

parts.note: suggests a warship, but means a man of a particular war, the one fought in South Africa

explanation.definitionFit: A Boer was a Dutch-descended South African who fought the British in the Boer War.

clue.text: Flag for CND supporter?

definitions.meaning: someone who would ban the bomb, as the Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament wants

explanation.walkthrough: CND is the UK Campaign for Nuclear Disarmament, whose slogan was Ban the Bomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner is a flag, and whimsically one who bans things.

clue.text: Push the boat out and depart

definitions.meaning: literally, push off from the shore

explanation.definitionFit: Shove off means to push a boat from the bank, and informally to leave.
